brief.prompt:
I want to learn to build this project: Tutoring requests and follow-up. I am starting from zero. Use everyday words and explain each action before asking me to do it.

WHAT I HAVE
{
  "id": "TUT-01",
  "student": "Student A",
  "topic": "Study plan",
  "preferredTime": ""
}

WHAT IT MEANS
student uses a fictional name; topic is the subject; preferredTime is a suitable time for the student.

WHAT I SHOULD ACHIEVE
The student wants help with a study plan but supplied no time. Prepare a question asking for that missing detail.

MY SITUATION
I work at [MY CENTRE]. I will use [TOOL]. [REVIEWER] will check the work. First use this fictional example; later we will replace it with my project details. Ask me when information is missing and wait for an answer. Do not fill in dates, prices, permissions or answers yourself.

HELP ME IN THIS ORDER
1. Explain the problem through an everyday situation. Describe what I would have in front of me before starting and what I would see at the end. Explain any technical word in the same sentence.
2. Solve the example using the details supplied. Show the complete result, not a list of tips. Point to the detail supporting each decision. If a person must review something, state the question they need to answer.
3. Guide me through repeating it myself. Use numbered steps. For each step, say which application to open, which document or screen to find, what to copy and what should appear next. Do not simply say “configure the system”. If you do not know my version’s controls, ask for their names instead of inventing a location.
4. Prepare a small table with: example number, what we received, what we will do, who reviews it and its current state. Leave the reviewer blank if I have not named them. Do not mark an action done until I confirm I performed it.
5. Suggest a second example changing just one detail. Explain what should change and what should remain the same. Then show an example missing a required detail and explain how to ask for it.
6. If automation would save copying, explain the manual route first and the automatic route second. Identify what the practice actually does and which real connection is still needed. Showing a result in n8n is different from saving it to a spreadsheet or sending a message.
7. Help me adapt the example to my centre. Ask for one small case, explain which rule changes and keep the first version so I can return to it.

AT THE END
Leave a simple document containing the original example, worked answer, steps I repeated, errors I found and the next step. Include a check another person can carry out without reading this conversation. Do not treat an attractive document as proof that the project works.

needs: An n8n account or installation you can open.

parameters.jsCode: const seen = new Set(); return $input.all().map(item => { const x = item.json; if (typeof x.id !== 'string' || !x.id.trim()) throw new Error('Missing id'); const sample = {"id":"TUT-01","student":"Student A","topic":"Study plan","preferredTime":""}; for (const [key,value] of Object.entries(sample)) { if (!(key in x)) throw new Error('Missing field: '+key); if (value !== null && typeof x[key] !== typeof value) throw new Error('Wrong type: '+key); if (typeof value === 'number' && (!Number.isFinite(x[key]) || x[key] < 0)) throw new Error('Invalid number: '+key); } if (seen.has(x.id)) throw new Error('Repeated id in this run'); seen.add(x.id); return item; });
return $input.all().map(item => { const x = item.json; return { json: { ...x, result: x.preferredTime.trim() ? "ready" : "review" } }; });
return $input.all().map(item => ({ json: { ...item.json, practiceOnly: true, savedExternally: false } }));

careful: Import the file, run it and open the last box. The result remains inside n8n.
For “Tutoring requests and follow-up”, confirm who reviews a decision before it takes effect. Practising an answer is not approval to purchase, return an item or confirm a booking.

To save the n8n result, first create a test sheet with id, result, reviewedBy and approved columns. Add Google Sheets at the end and connect your account under credentials. Choose Append or Update Row, select the document and sheet, and use id as the matching column. Map each column to the same-named value from the previous box. Run one example, open the sheet and check its values.

Repeat the same number: this practice should update its row. Then try another number. A spreadsheet cannot guarantee preventing duplicates when several runs write at once; for that use, arrange a database that enforces unique numbers. Add real notifications after checking saving and review.

Also test leaving a required field empty. The workflow checks that all example fields exist and have the correct data type. Before daily use, add your centre’s rules, such as possible dates and allowed quantities, and a route to request missing details. Write down how to stop the process and where to continue manually.
